papers.title: TP-JSCC: Efficient Token Pruning and Joint Source-Channel Coding for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration
papers.abstract_en: Deploying large vision-language models (LVLMs) on resource-constrained embodied agents for 3D visual question answering necessitates cloud-edge collaboration. However, offloading massive visual data to the cloud over bandwidth-limited and noisy channels introduces severe latency and transmission distortion. To address this, we propose TP-JSCC, an efficient token pruning and joint source-channel coding method for LVLMs-based 3D-VQA in Cloud-Edge Collaboration. First, we develop a Local and Global Semantics-based Hybrid Token Pruning (LGS-HTP) module to significantly reduce the visual token count. By decoupling foreground-background tokens and jointly selecting local and global semantics, LGS-HTP effectively reduces redundancy while preserving reasoning-critical tokens. Second, we introduce a lightweight Token Joint Source-Channel Coding (T-JSCC) module to further compress the pruned tokens and ensure their robust transmission over error-prone channels. By employing lightweight cascaded linear layers and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR)-adaptive mechanism, this module adapts to fluctuating channel conditions while maintaining minimal computational overhead. Extensive experiments on ScanQA and SQA3D datasets indicate the exceptional efficiency and robustness of our approach. Specifically, on ScanQA validation set, the LGS-HTP module could achieve 90% pruning ratio while incurring less than a 1% CIDEr loss. Building on this, the T-JSCC further compresses the tokens by 18 times, resulting in an overall 180 times data volume reduction for robust transmission, while saving 90% in computational complexity for LVLM deployment. Our code is available at https://github.com/yuanhui0325/TP-JSCC.
papers.abstract_zh: 在资源受限的具身智能体上部署大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）以进行 3D 视觉问答，需要云边协同。然而，在带宽受限且含噪信道上将海量视觉数据卸载到云端会带来严重延迟和传输失真。为此，我们提出 TP-JSCC，一种面向云边协同中基于 LVLM 的 3D-VQA 的高效 token 剪枝与联合信源信道编码方法。首先，我们开发基于局部与全局语义的混合 token 剪枝（LGS-HTP）模块，以显著减少视觉 token 数量。通过解耦前景-背景 token 并联合选择局部与全局语义，LGS-HTP 在保留推理关键 token 的同时有效减少冗余。其次，我们引入轻量级 token 联合信源信道编码（T-JSCC）模块，进一步压缩剪枝后的 token 并确保其在易错信道上稳健传输。通过采用轻量级级联线性层和信噪比（SNR）自适应机制，该模块在保持极低计算开销的同时适应波动的信道条件。在 ScanQA 和 SQA3D 数据集上的大量实验表明我们的方法具有出色的效率与鲁棒性。具体而言，在 ScanQA 验证集上，LGS-HTP 模块可实现 90% 的剪枝率，而 CIDEr 损失低于 1%。在此基础上，T-JSCC 进一步将 token 压缩 18 倍，实现总体 180 倍的数据量缩减以进行稳健传输，同时为 LVLM 部署节省 90% 的计算复杂度。代码见 https://github.com/yuanhui0325/TP-JSCC。
papers.tldr_zh: TP-JSCC 通过局部-全局语义混合 token 剪枝与 SNR 自适应的轻量联合信源信道编码，在 ScanQA 上以 90% 剪枝率保持 CIDEr 损失低于 1%，并实现 180 倍数据量缩减与 90% 计算复杂度节省。

papers.title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions
papers.abstract_en: Fine-grained visual perception remains a bottleneck during post-training of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), as perceptual errors can constrain gains from reasoning-focused optimization. Although image-caption pre-training improves perception, its influence can weaken as subsequent stages change data mixtures and objectives. Continuing caption supervision during post-training is challenging because subjective, information-dense descriptions complicate verifiable reward design. We present PerceptRL, which strengthens perception at two complementary levels. Perception RL uses a multi-agent pipeline to extract verified errors from dense image captions and convert the corresponding visual facts into QA pairs with fixed answer labels and rule-based rewards. Chain QA links correlated errors, while multiple-choice QA combines unrelated errors. A specialized route targets high-error domains with tailored verification, and a domain-agnostic general route covers errors beyond these domains. Perception Agentic RL addresses fine-grained and dense cases unresolved by single-turn Perception RL through multi-turn inspection with visual tools. We observe coordinate drift even in models trained to use tools, where incorrect crops or annotations distort evidence and propagate errors. Coordinate Injection corrects spatial operations in cold-start trajectories, while a grounding-aware process reward supervises intermediate spatial fidelity alongside final-answer correctness. Training proceeds through shared cold-start SFT, single-turn Perception RL, and multi-turn Perception Agentic RL. Across seven benchmarks under a shared tool-use protocol, PerceptRL achieves 71.6% average accuracy, surpassing the base model with the same tools and the strongest evaluated frontier VLM by 15.7 and 5.2 percentage points, respectively.
papers.abstract_zh: 在多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）的后训练阶段，细粒度视觉感知仍是瓶颈，因为感知错误会限制以推理为中心的优化所带来的收益。尽管图像描述预训练能改善感知，但随着后续阶段改变数据混合与目标，其影响可能减弱。在后训练期间继续描述监督具有挑战性，因为主观且信息密集的描述使可验证奖励设计变得复杂。我们提出 PerceptRL，从两个互补层面增强感知。感知强化学习（Perception RL）使用多智能体流水线从密集图像描述中提取经核验的错误，并将相应视觉事实转换为具有固定答案标签和基于规则奖励的问答对。链式问答（Chain QA）连接相关错误，而多项选择问答（multiple-choice QA）组合不相关错误。专门路线针对高错误领域进行定制化验证，领域无关的通用路线覆盖这些领域之外的错误。感知智能体强化学习（Perception Agentic RL）通过使用视觉工具的多轮检查，处理单轮 Perception RL 未能解决的细粒度与密集情形。我们观察到，即使在训练为使用工具的模型中也会出现坐标漂移，其中不正确的裁剪或标注会扭曲证据并传播错误。坐标注入（Coordinate Injection）在冷启动轨迹中纠正空间操作，而具备定位感知的过程奖励在监督最终答案正确性的同时监督中间空间保真度。训练依次经过共享冷启动 SFT、单轮 Perception RL 和多轮 Perception Agentic RL。在共享工具使用协议下的七个基准上，PerceptRL 达到 71.6% 的平均准确率，分别比使用相同工具的基模型和评估中最强的前沿 VLM 高出 15.7 和 5.2 个百分点。
papers.tldr_zh: PerceptRL 通过从密集图像描述中提取可验证错误构建问答奖励，并结合多轮工具检查与坐标注入的过程奖励，在七个基准上取得 71.6% 平均准确率。

papers.title: CoS-VQ: Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization for Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) require substantial memory, motivating low-bit weight quantization for efficient deployment. Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods often improve accuracy by increasing the effective coding dimension, which can complicate independent lookup and local codeword updates. We propose CoS-VQ (Coordinated Shared-Scale Vector Quantization), which preserves low-dimensional codewords while jointly optimizing hard indices and their shared scale across positions. The key challenge is scale-induced coupling: the optimal scale depends on the entire codeword combination and, in turn, changes candidate rankings across positions, so pointwise updates can stall even after scale re-optimization. CoS-VQ collects candidates at multiple probe scales and constructs a tangent separable upper bound for the residual-aware quadratic objective. By reducing candidate comparisons to lower envelopes of lines over positive scales, it identifies finitely many representative intervals for joint index--scale updates without exhaustively enumerating codeword combinations. On Qwen3.8-27B, CoS-VQ outperforms QTIP and LLVQ on the evaluated language modeling, coding, and reasoning benchmarks. Ablations from the same initialization further show larger gains from joint updates than from scale-only refinement, highlighting joint selection as an alternative to increasing codeword dimensionality. The code is available at https://github.com/xzktx003/Cos_VQ.
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLMs）需要大量内存，这推动了低比特权重量化以实现高效部署。现有向量量化（VQ）方法通常通过增加有效编码维度来提高准确率，但这可能使独立查找和局部码字更新变得复杂。我们提出 CoS-VQ（协调共享尺度向量量化），它在保留低维码字的同时，联合优化硬索引及其跨位置的共享尺度。关键挑战是尺度诱导的耦合：最优尺度取决于整个码字组合，进而改变跨位置的候选排序，因此即使重新优化尺度，逐点更新也可能停滞。CoS-VQ 在多个探测尺度上收集候选，并为残差感知的二次目标构造切线可分离上界。通过将候选比较简化为正尺度上直线的下包络，它识别出有限多个代表性区间，从而在不穷举码字组合的情况下进行联合索引—尺度更新。在 Qwen3.8-27B 上，CoS-VQ 在评估的语言建模、编码和推理基准上优于 QTIP 和 LLVQ。来自相同初始化的消融进一步表明，联合更新比仅尺度细化带来更大收益，突显联合选择可作为增加码字维度的替代方案。代码见 https://github.com/xzktx003/Cos_VQ。
papers.tldr_zh: CoS-VQ 在低维码字下联合优化硬索引与共享尺度，通过切线可分离上界避免穷举组合，在 Qwen3.8-27B 上优于 QTIP 和 LLVQ。

papers.title: Training-Free Inference Acceleration for Video Large Language Models: Methods, Trade-offs, and Evaluation
papers.abstract_en: Video Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in video understanding and reasoning, but processing long visual sequences incurs substantial computational, latency, and memory overhead. This survey examines training-free inference acceleration, focusing on reducing inference costs while preserving task-relevant spatiotemporal evidence. We organize existing methods by their intervention stages in the inference pipeline, covering input, visual encoding, projector, prefill, and decoding. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is discussed separately as a cross-stage extension with varying calibration requirements. We analyze how intervention position affects evidence preservation and computational savings, and why local efficiency improvements may not translate into end-to-end acceleration. We complement this analysis with quantitative evidence from prior studies and our own experiments under a shared evaluation setting to assess accuracy-latency trade-offs.
papers.abstract_zh: 视频大语言模型（VLMs）在视频理解与推理方面展现出强大能力，但处理长视觉序列会带来大量计算、延迟和内存开销。本综述考察免训练推理加速，重点是在保留任务相关时空证据的同时降低推理成本。我们按推理流水线中的干预阶段组织现有方法，涵盖输入、视觉编码、投影器、预填充和解码。训练后量化（PTQ）作为具有不同校准要求的跨阶段扩展单独讨论。我们分析干预位置如何影响证据保留与计算节省，以及为何局部效率提升可能无法转化为端到端加速。我们结合先前研究的定量证据以及我们在共享评估设置下进行的实验来补充这一分析，以评估准确率—延迟权衡。
papers.tldr_zh: 该综述按输入、视觉编码、投影器、预填充和解码等干预阶段梳理视频大语言模型的免训练推理加速方法，并分析准确率与延迟的权衡。

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
papers.abstract_en: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. To do so, we propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate. By systematically varying SynthAPI's generation controls in 458,752 tasks across 849 trained models of four different sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of the synthesized environments. These predictable relationships reveal several lessons for scaling tool-use agent data. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains. Scaling according to these findings yields agents that outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation across four evaluation benchmarks.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们探索如何构建能够完成复杂多步任务的高性能大语言模型（LLM）工具使用智能体。具体而言，我们研究合成生成的工具使用环境中的数据组成如何影响此类智能体的训练。为此，我们提出 SynthAPI 流水线，它沿工具、任务以及工具所操作数据库的轴显式控制生成环境的多样性。通过在 458,752 个任务、849 个四种不同规模的训练模型中系统改变 SynthAPI 的生成控制，我们推导出一个缩放定律，根据合成环境的规模与组成预测下游工具使用智能体的泛化能力。这些可预测的关系揭示了扩展工具使用智能体数据的若干经验。随着数据预算增长，扩展工具和数据库多样性比增加任务数量更有效，而提高数据复杂度会带来更大收益。根据这些发现进行扩展所得到的智能体，在四个评估基准上优于使用先前工作在工具使用智能体与合成环境生成方面数据训练的模型。
papers.tldr_zh: SynthAPI 通过可控合成工具使用环境并训练 849 个模型，推导出预测智能体泛化的缩放定律，发现扩展工具与数据库多样性比增加任务数更有效。

papers.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract_en: We propose Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni (NLD-Uni), a unified discrete diffusion large language model (DLLM) for visual understanding and generation tasks. Compared with prior unified diffusion models, NLD-Uni introduces two major innovations. First, we propose a unified cross-paradigm on-policy distillation (OPD) framework that successfully transfers the visual understanding ability of autoregressive VLMs and visual generation ability of continuous flow models, to a unified DLLM. Second, NLD-Uni incorporates a novel progressive self-refining diffusion process that gradually corrupts each token across multiple steps during training, as opposed to adopting the conventional masked diffusion formulation that directly corrupts a clean image token to an uninformative mask token. At inference, this design allows NLD-Uni to make intermediate commit to a token, enabling progressive self-refinement for better visual quality. Through extensive experiments, we show that NLD-Uni achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified DLLMs on diverse tasks including visual question-answering, multi-modal reasoning, object grounding, text-to-image generation, and image editing.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出 Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni（NLD-Uni），一种用于视觉理解与生成任务的统一离散扩散大语言模型（DLLM）。与先前统一扩散模型相比，NLD-Uni 引入两项主要创新。第一，我们提出统一的跨范式在策略蒸馏（OPD）框架，成功将自回归 VLM 的视觉理解能力和连续流模型的视觉生成能力迁移到统一的 DLLM。第二，NLD-Uni 采用新颖的渐进自细化扩散过程，在训练中跨多个步骤逐步破坏每个 token，而非采用直接将干净图像 token 破坏为无信息掩码 token 的传统掩码扩散形式。在推理时，该设计允许 NLD-Uni 对 token 进行中间提交，从而实现渐进自细化以获得更好的视觉质量。通过大量实验，我们表明 NLD-Uni 在视觉问答、多模态推理、目标定位、文本到图像生成和图像编辑等多样任务上，在统一 DLLM 中达到最先进性能。
papers.tldr_zh: NLD-Uni 通过跨范式在策略蒸馏与渐进自细化扩散，将自回归 VLM 的理解能力和连续流模型的生成能力统一到离散扩散 LLM 中。

papers.title: TUON: A Tensor-Aware Optimizer Utilizing Tensor-SVD and Polarization for Large Language Model Pretraining
papers.abstract_en: Large scale language model~(LLM) pretraining is increasingly bottlenecked by optimizer efficiency, driving optimizer design from vector-aware methods such as AdamW to matrix-aware methods. Matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon exploit matrix structure but treat layers independently, neglecting cross-layer correlations. Tensor-aware optimizers are therefore needed, yet existing ones rely on a matricization-based tensor algebra and remain restricted to shallow stacking and specific modules. In this paper, we propose \textbf{TUON}, a novel optimizer built on a transform-based tensor algebra derived from the Tensor-SVD (T-SVD). Unlike methods that polarize a globally unfolded matrix, TUON mixes layers via a unitary transform $\boldsymbol{Q}$ and then polarizes each transformed slice, and inverts the transform to recover the update. This mix-then-separate strategy captures cross-layer correlations while preserving per-layer diversity, avoiding the structural dimension imbalance and cross-layer misalignment of unfolding. Thus it successfully scales to more layers and diverse modules beyond QKV. Theoretically, we prove that TUON performs steepest descent under a $\boldsymbol{Q}$-transformed tensor spectral norm, and identify its update as the tensor polar factor of the T-SVD. We further establish transform non-redundancy, norm and smoothness comparisons with Muon and TEON, and a convergence guarantee. Empirically, TUON improves consistently over Muon and TEON on GPT-124M/350M and Qwen-0.6B/4B, with ablations confirming the transformation mechanism, cross-layer structure beyond two-layer stacking, adaptability beyond QKV, and robustness to the polarization method.
papers.abstract_zh: 大规模语言模型（LLM）预训练日益受优化器效率制约，推动优化器设计从 AdamW 等向量感知方法转向矩阵感知方法。Muon 等矩阵感知优化器利用矩阵结构，但独立处理各层，忽略了跨层相关性。因此需要张量感知优化器，然而现有方法依赖基于矩阵化的张量代数，且仍局限于浅层堆叠和特定模块。本文提出 TUON，一种基于由张量奇异值分解（T-SVD）导出的基于变换的张量代数的新型优化器。与对全局展开矩阵进行极化的方法不同，TUON 通过酉变换 Q 混合各层，然后对每个变换后的切片进行极化，并逆变换以恢复更新。这种先混合后分离的策略在捕捉跨层相关性的同时保留各层多样性，避免了展开带来的结构维度失衡和跨层错位。因此它能成功扩展到更多层以及 QKV 之外的多样模块。理论上，我们证明 TUON 在 Q 变换后的张量谱范数下执行最速下降，并确认其更新为 T-SVD 的张量极因子。我们进一步建立了变换非冗余性、与 Muon 和 TEON 的范数与平滑性比较，以及收敛保证。实验上，TUON 在 GPT-124M/350M 和 Qwen-0.6B/4B 上持续优于 Muon 和 TEON，消融实验证实了变换机制、超越两层堆叠的跨层结构、超越 QKV 的适应性以及对极化方法的鲁棒性。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于 T-SVD 变换张量代数的优化器 TUON，通过酉变换混合各层后逐切片极化再逆变换，在捕捉跨层相关性的同时保留层间多样性，理论上证明其为张量谱范数下的最速下降并给出收敛保证，在 GPT-124M/350M 与 Qwen-0.6B/4B 上持续优于 Muon 和 TEON。

papers.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
papers.abstract_en: Video captioning aims to preserve visual information through compact descriptions, predominantly using natural language. However, precisely expressing fine-grained spatial structures and temporal dynamics in natural language often leads to lengthy and potentially ambiguous descriptions. In this work, we explore Code as Video Caption, a paradigm where executable programs serve as a complementary representation of visual content through graphical primitives, layout rules, and functions of time. To examine whether code captions effectively preserve video information, we compare them with natural language captions on downstream question answering and video reconstruction tasks. Our results show that code captions achieve superior reasoning accuracy and reconstruction fidelity. Despite these advantages, realizing the potential of code captioning depends on whether current multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate faithful code captions. To systematically assess this capability, we introduce CodeCap-Bench, which comprises 323 videos spanning five categories of structured 2D content, along with fine-grained annotations and a multi-level evaluation framework. Extensive experiments reveal that while leading proprietary MLLMs demonstrate promising code captioning capabilities, they still struggle to faithfully capture complex temporal dynamics, with open-source models lagging substantially behind.
papers.abstract_zh: 视频描述旨在通过紧凑的描述保留视觉信息，主要使用自然语言。然而，用自然语言精确表达细粒度空间结构和时间动态往往会导致描述冗长且可能产生歧义。在本工作中，我们探索“代码作为视频描述”（Code as Video Caption）这一范式，其中可执行程序通过图形基元、布局规则和时间函数，作为视觉内容的补充表示。为检验代码描述是否能有效保留视频信息，我们在下游问答和视频重建任务上将其与自然语言描述进行比较。结果表明，代码描述在推理准确性和重建保真度上均更优。尽管有这些优势，实现代码描述潜力的前提是当前多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）能否生成忠实的代码描述。为系统评估这一能力，我们提出 CodeCap-Bench，包含 323 个视频，覆盖五类结构化 2D 内容，并配有细粒度标注和多层次评估框架。大量实验表明，尽管领先的专有 MLLMs 展现出有前景的代码描述能力，但它们仍难以忠实捕捉复杂的时间动态，开源模型则明显落后。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出以可执行程序作为视频描述的补充表示，并构建 CodeCap-Bench 评估多模态大模型生成忠实代码描述的能力。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment

papers.title: Watermark Basins: Black-Box Detection of Distilled LLMs
papers.abstract_en: Proprietary language models and their reasoning traces are vulnerable to API-based distillation, where an adversary trains a student model on the teacher model's outputs. To obtain evidence of distillation, model providers can watermark the teacher's outputs, aiming to leave a radioactive signal in the student's outputs. Existing black-box detectors search for such radioactivity using token-level statistics of the suspect model's outputs. However, token-level signals are not always detectable, for instance when the distillation traces are sampled at a low temperature. In this work, we discover the watermark basin, a persistent signal that enables more reliable watermark detection: during fine-tuning, watermarked teacher traces embed a distinct, key-specific geometric signal in parameter space that lies orthogonal to the ordinary task-specific fine-tuning subspace. Building on this, we introduce Watermark Basin Alignment (WM-Basin), a black-box watermark detector that queries the suspect model through its API, without access to its weights or logits. WM-Basin maps generated text to gradient representations using a fixed clean probe model, projects out the ordinary fine-tuning task directions, and tests whether the residual gradient aligns with the watermark basin induced by the watermark key. We evaluate WM-Basin extensively across diverse teacher models and student architectures (from 135M to 8.2B parameters) distilled on mathematical reasoning. At a strict 0.1% false-positive rate, WM-Basin detects 79% of distilled models at n-gram=1 and 45% at n-gram=3, substantially improving over the state-of-the-art token-level baseline (29% and 1.3%, respectively). Because the watermark signal resides in a persistent basin, it survives post-distillation modifications including quantization, pruning, and reinforcement-learning post-training.
papers.abstract_zh: 专有语言模型及其推理轨迹容易受到基于 API 的蒸馏攻击，即对手利用教师模型的输出训练学生模型。为获取蒸馏证据，模型提供方可以对教师输出添加水印，旨在在学生输出中留下放射性信号。现有黑盒检测器利用可疑模型输出的 token 级统计来搜索此类放射性。然而，token 级信号并非总能被检测到，例如当蒸馏轨迹以较低温度采样时。在本工作中，我们发现水印盆地（watermark basin），一种能够实现更可靠水印检测的持久信号：在微调过程中，带水印的教师轨迹会在参数空间中嵌入一个独特的、与密钥相关的几何信号，该信号与普通任务特定微调子空间正交。基于此，我们提出水印盆地对齐（Watermark Basin Alignment, WM-Basin），一种通过 API 查询可疑模型、无需访问其权重或 logits 的黑盒水印检测器。WM-Basin 使用固定的干净探针模型将生成文本映射为梯度表示，投影去除普通微调任务方向，并检验残差梯度是否与由水印密钥诱导的水印盆地对齐。我们在数学推理蒸馏的多种教师模型和学生架构（135M 至 8.2B 参数）上广泛评估 WM-Basin。在严格的 0.1% 假阳性率下，WM-Basin 在 n-gram=1 时检测出 79% 的蒸馏模型，在 n-gram=3 时检测出 45%，显著优于最先进的 token 级基线（分别为 29% 和 1.3%）。由于水印信号位于持久盆地中，它能在蒸馏后的量化、剪枝和强化学习后训练等修改中存活。
papers.tldr_zh: 发现蒸馏微调会在参数空间中留下与任务子空间正交的持久“水印盆地”，据此提出黑盒检测器 WM-Basin，在低假阳性率下显著优于 token 级基线。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training

papers.title: LearnPrunerV2: Learnable Progressive Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated remarkable multimodal capabilities but suffer from prohibitive computational overhead due to the massive number of visual tokens. While token pruning is a promising solution, existing methods still suffer from two major drawbacks: 1) unreliable pruning criteria that fail to accurately localize task-specific regions due to inherent attention biases or query-agnostic designs, and 2) suboptimal pruning strategies that employ rigid, non-adaptive schedules, overlooking the dynamic evolution of token redundancy across different model depths. To address these challenges, we propose LearnPrunerV2, which extends the previous two-stage heuristic framework (LearnPruner) into a fully learnable architecture. Specifically, we integrate lightweight learnable modules into every layer of the VLM backbone, which estimate token importance by fusing intrinsic visual saliency with extrinsic query relevance captured via a shadow token. By uncovering a consistent staircase redundancy pattern across VLM layers, we further introduce Budget-Deterministic Pruning (BDP) to establish a hardware-friendly schedule with fixed per-layer budgets. Extensive experimental results across various benchmarks and VLMs demonstrate that LearnPrunerV2 consistently outperform previous state-of-the-art methods. Notably, LearnPrunerV2 preserves 99.8% of the original performance when pruning 77.8% of visual tokens on LLaVA-v1.5, achieving a superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）已展现出卓越的多模态能力，但由于海量视觉 token 而承受着高昂的计算开销。token 剪枝是一种有前景的解决方案，但现有方法仍存在两大缺陷：1）不可靠的剪枝准则，由于固有的注意力偏差或与查询无关的设计，无法准确定位任务特定区域；2）次优的剪枝策略，采用僵化、非自适应的调度，忽视了 token 冗余在不同模型深度上的动态演变。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 LearnPrunerV2，将先前的两阶段启发式框架（LearnPruner）扩展为完全可学习的架构。具体而言，我们在 VLM 主干网络的每一层中集成轻量级可学习模块，通过融合内在视觉显著性与经由影子 token 捕获的外在查询相关性来估计 token 重要性。通过揭示 VLM 各层中一致的阶梯式冗余模式，我们进一步引入预算确定性剪枝（Budget-Deterministic Pruning, BDP），以建立具有固定逐层预算的硬件友好调度。跨多种基准和 VLM 的大量实验结果表明，LearnPrunerV2 持续优于先前的最先进方法。值得注意的是，在 LLaVA-v1.5 上剪枝 77.8% 的视觉 token 时，LearnPrunerV2 保留了原始性能的 99.8%，实现了更优的精度-效率权衡。
papers.tldr_zh: 将两阶段启发式 token 剪枝扩展为逐层可学习架构，并结合固定逐层预算的剪枝调度，在 LLaVA-v1.5 上剪去 77.8% 视觉 token 仍保留 99.8% 性能。

evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：state-of-the-art, extensive experiment

papers.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: A vulnerability costs more to fix the later it is discovered. As coding agents generate code faster than developers can review it, software needs a first line of defense screening each new function in real time. LLM agents have recently become capable of finding real-world vulnerabilities by working as a security expert would: they run analysis tools, explore the surrounding code, test hypotheses and weigh the evidence before forming their own judgement. This reasoning, however, spans many model calls, so that each verdict takes minutes of compute, far too long for real-time screening. Faster detectors, which fine-tune deep learning models or prompt an LLM for a direct verdict, are less accurate: they judge a function without the context an agent gathers, and an LLM's generated verdict is unreliable even when given some of it. We present REVA (REal-time Vulnerability Analysis), an AI vulnerability detector that brings the security context and code understanding components behind agentic detectors into a single forward pass of an LLM. For each new function, REVA gives the LLM a pre-computed threat model of its module, lightweight static analysis findings and call-graph information. REVA leverages a trained probe to read the LLM's internal representations of the new function in this context. On PrimeVul's held-out test set, REVA on GLM-5.3-Flash reaches 60.0% accuracy in about one second per function. This matches VulTriage (59.2%), the state-of-the-art agentic detector, run on the same LLM, while being over 250 times faster and less than a tenth as costly. On the same prompt, the probe is 14% to 17% more accurate than the LLM's own direct verdict. Across three open LLMs, REVA is at least as accurate as VulTriage, and about 10% more accurate on two of them. An LLM's internal representations thus encode much of what agentic detectors obtain through reasoning.
papers.abstract_zh: 漏洞发现得越晚，修复成本越高。随着编码智能体生成代码的速度超过开发者审查的速度，软件需要一道实时筛查每个新函数的第一道防线。LLM 智能体近来已能够像安全专家那样发现真实世界漏洞：它们运行分析工具、探索周边代码、检验假设并权衡证据，然后形成自己的判断。然而，这种推理跨越多次模型调用，因此每个判定需要数分钟的计算，对于实时筛查而言过于漫长。更快的检测器——微调深度学习模型或提示 LLM 直接给出判定——准确性较低：它们在判断函数时缺乏智能体所收集的上下文，而即使提供部分上下文，LLM 生成的判定也不可靠。我们提出 REVA（REal-time Vulnerability Analysis），一种 AI 漏洞检测器，将智能体检测器背后的安全上下文和代码理解组件整合进 LLM 的单次前向传播。对于每个新函数，REVA 向 LLM 提供其模块的预计算威胁模型、轻量级静态分析发现和调用图信息。REVA 利用训练好的探针读取 LLM 在此上下文中对新函数内部表示的解读。在 PrimeVul 的留出测试集上，基于 GLM-5.3-Flash 的 REVA 在每个函数约一秒内达到 60.0% 的准确率。这与在同一 LLM 上运行的最先进智能体检测器 VulTriage（59.2%）相当，同时速度快 250 倍以上，成本不到其十分之一。在相同提示下，探针比 LLM 自身的直接判定准确率高 14% 至 17%。在三个开源 LLM 上，REVA 至少与 VulTriage 一样准确，在其中两个上约高 10%。因此，LLM 的内部表示编码了智能体检测器通过推理所获得的大部分信息。
papers.tldr_zh: 将威胁模型、静态分析与调用图上下文注入单次前向传播，并用探针读取 LLM 内部表示，实现约一秒内完成漏洞检测，准确率与智能体检测器相当但快 250 倍以上。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Robust LLM Data Selection via Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution
papers.abstract_en: Gradient-based data attribution has become an important tool for high-quality data selection in the instruction fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs), as it estimates the contribution of training examples through their influence on model optimization. However, we find that existing global gradient attribution methods suffer from surface-form bias: minor changes to semantically irrelevant details, such as wording or formatting, can produce highly inconsistent attribution scores even when the underlying content remains unchanged. To address this issue, we propose Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution (CIGA), a robust framework for instruction data selection. CIGA first identifies layers whose gradients are both influential for attribution and stable under semantics-preserving surface-form perturbations, thereby reducing formatting noise in gradient features. It then dynamically fuses these attribution signals with semantic representations of the input, combining optimization-level influence with content-level information. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks show that CIGA produces more stable rankings under surface-form perturbations while preserving downstream capabilities and improving average performance. CIGA also reduces attribution cost, offering a robust and efficient approach to data selection for LLM instruction tuning.
papers.abstract_zh: 基于梯度的数据归因已成为大语言模型（LLMs）指令微调中高质量数据选择的重要工具，因为它通过训练样本对模型优化的影响来估计其贡献。然而，我们发现现有的全局梯度归因方法存在表面形式偏差：对语义无关细节（如措辞或格式）的微小改动，即使底层内容保持不变，也可能产生高度不一致的归因分数。为解决这一问题，我们提出内容不变梯度归因（Content-Invariant Gradient Attribution, CIGA），一个用于指令数据选择的稳健框架。CIGA 首先识别那些对归因既有影响力、又在保持语义的表面形式扰动下稳定的层，从而减少梯度特征中的格式噪声。然后，它将归因信号与输入的语义表示动态融合，结合优化层面的影响与内容层面的信息。跨多个基准的大量实验表明，CIGA 在表面形式扰动下产生更稳定的排序，同时保持下游能力并提升平均性能。CIGA 还降低了归因成本，为 LLM 指令微调的数据选择提供了一种稳健且高效的方法。
papers.tldr_zh: 针对梯度归因的表面形式偏差，提出内容不变梯度归因 CIGA，筛选稳定层并融合语义表示，使数据选择排序更稳定且提升下游平均性能。

匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning

papers.title: Test-Time Confidence Adaptation under RL-Induced Trajectory Shift
papers.abstract_en: Trajectory-based confidence estimation has shown promising performance for large language models (LLMs) by leveraging rich signals from their reasoning processes. However, we find that such confidence estimators can degrade substantially after agentic reinforcement learning (Agentic RL) as it induces substantial shifts in the reasoning trajectories. More importantly, despite these shifts, we uncover a reliability structure that is largely preserved across Base and RL models: $\textbf{more}$ $\textbf{stable}$ $\textbf{trajectories}$ $\textbf{remain}$ $\textbf{more}$ $\textbf{likely}$ $\textbf{to}$ $\textbf{produce}$ $\textbf{correct}$ $\textbf{answers}$. This preserved relationship provides a transferable, label-free reliability signal for post-RL confidence adaptation. Building on this finding, we propose $\textbf{StaR-TTA}$, a stability-guided framework for label-free test-time confidence adaptation. StaR-TTA jointly learns from correctness supervision and stability-derived reliability supervision on labeled Base trajectories, establishing the connection between trajectory stability and answer reliability. At test time, it reuses stability-induced reliability rankings from unlabeled RL trajectories to adapt confidence scores to the shifted trajectory distribution, without requiring target correctness labels. Across four QA benchmarks, StaR-TTA achieves an average AUROC of \(0.721\), with consistent improvements across unseen datasets, model families and scales, and different Agentic RL algorithms.
papers.abstract_zh: 基于轨迹的置信度估计通过利用大语言模型（LLM）推理过程中的丰富信号，已展现出良好性能。然而，我们发现，在智能体强化学习（Agentic RL）之后，此类置信度估计器可能显著退化，因为 Agentic RL 会引起推理轨迹的显著偏移。更重要的是，尽管存在这些偏移，我们揭示了一种在 Base 模型与 RL 模型之间基本得以保留的可靠性结构：更稳定的轨迹仍然更可能产生正确答案。这一被保留的关系为 RL 后的置信度自适应提供了一种可迁移、无需标签的可靠性信号。基于这一发现，我们提出 StaR-TTA，一个以稳定性为引导、无需标签的测试时置信度自适应框架。StaR-TTA 在有标签的 Base 轨迹上同时从正确性监督和由稳定性导出的可靠性监督中学习，建立轨迹稳定性与答案可靠性之间的联系。在测试时，它复用来自无标签 RL 轨迹的稳定性诱导可靠性排序，使置信度分数适应偏移后的轨迹分布，而无需目标正确性标签。在四个问答基准上，StaR-TTA 取得平均 AUROC 0.721，并在未见数据集、不同模型家族与规模以及不同 Agentic RL 算法上均有一致提升。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文发现轨迹稳定性与答案正确性的关系在 Agentic RL 前后基本保留，据此提出无需标签的测试时置信度自适应框架 StaR-TTA，在四个问答基准上平均 AUROC 达 0.721。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
evidence: 明确的方法贡献：we propose, algorithm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
papers.abstract_en: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness. We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning, followed by supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach it how to move the robot. Without observing real-world robot data during training, ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness and outperforming the MolmoAct2 VLA (33.3%), while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Furthermore, ZAP also generalizes to an unseen embodiment as well as new objects, goals and strategies never seen during training. On a single-arm Franka, ZAP reaches 55.9% on RoboLab-120, 4.9 percentage points ahead of the leading VLA/WAM baseline.
papers.abstract_zh: 机器人策略需要理解场景中任务要求什么，以及如何移动机器人以完成该任务。为实现这两项技能，我们提出 Zero-real Agent Policy（ZAP），一种通过简单工具框架教会现成小型视觉语言模型控制机器人的方法。我们使用预训练的 27B 参数模型来引导世界理解与推理，随后在简单模拟任务上进行监督微调和 GRPO，以教会它如何移动机器人。训练期间未观察真实世界机器人数据，ZAP 在真实世界任务上达到 96.7% 的成功率，在我们的框架中与 GPT-6 Astra 相当，并优于 MolmoAct2 VLA（33.3%），同时运行速度比 GPT-6 Astra 快 3 倍、成本低 17 倍。此外，ZAP 还能泛化到未见过的具身形态，以及训练中从未见过的新物体、目标和策略。在单臂 Franka 上，ZAP 在 RoboLab-120 上达到 55.9%，领先最佳 VLA/WAM 基线 4.9 个百分点。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文提出 ZAP，用预训练 27B 视觉语言模型经模拟任务监督微调与 GRPO 训练机器人策略，未用真实机器人数据即在真实任务上达 96.7% 成功率，并泛化到新具身、物体、目标与策略。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Can LLMs Reliably Grade Olympiad Proofs? A Study of Mathematical Verification with LLMs
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) have made remarkable progress on solving competition-level mathematics, yet their ability to verify natural-language mathematical proofs remains relatively underexplored. This gap is especially pronounced for Olympiad-level proofs, which require meticulous assessment of each claim in a long reasoning chain. Current proof verification thus primarily relies on expert inspection, which is costly to scale. In this paper, we present a systematic study of LLM-based verification in this setting. Specifically, we introduce a human-curated dataset of USAMO 2025 candidate solutions with expert grading, and conduct a broad evaluation of existing LLM verifiers across frontier models. We also propose TROJAN, an iterative self-critique pipeline for generating high-fidelity adversarial proofs at scale. Our comprehensive evaluation covers 20 models spanning seven metrics, two prompt styles, three inference methods, and three prompt templates, showing that state-of-the-art models still leave considerable room for improvement. To narrow this gap, we propose MABGrader, a Multi-Armed Bandit framework that reframes grading as arm selection over the discrete score space. MABGrader outperforms the SOTA ProofGrader by 26.4% in Quadratic Weighted Kappa and reduces grading error by 14%. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/aziksh-ospanov/TROJAN.
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）在求解竞赛级数学方面已取得显著进展，但其验证自然语言数学证明的能力仍相对缺乏探索。这一差距在奥赛级证明上尤为明显，因为此类证明需要对长推理链中的每一项断言进行细致评估。因此，当前的证明验证主要依赖专家人工检查，难以低成本扩展。本文对 LLM 在此场景下的验证进行系统研究。具体而言，我们引入一个经人工整理、由专家评分的 USAMO 2025 候选解答数据集，并对前沿模型中的现有 LLM 验证器进行广泛评估。我们还提出 TROJAN，一种迭代式自我批评流水线，用于大规模生成高保真对抗性证明。我们的综合评估覆盖 20 个模型、七项指标、两种提示风格、三种推理方法和三种提示模板，表明最先进模型仍有相当大的改进空间。为缩小这一差距，我们提出 MABGrader，一个多臂老虎机框架，将评分重新表述为在离散分数空间上的臂选择问题。MABGrader 在二次加权 Kappa 上比 SOTA 的 ProofGrader 高 26.4%，并将评分误差降低 14%。代码与数据集见 https://github.com/aziksh-ospanov/TROJAN。

papers.title: Joint Dynamic Lane Reversal and Variable Speed Limit Control: A Graphormer-Based Approach
papers.abstract_en: Connected and automated vehicles could allow reassigning lane directions and speed limits on every road frequently, but the benefit hinges on how traffic reroutes, and one-way roads can isolate junctions. We formulate network-wide dynamic lane allocation and directional speed limit control with one-way roads, lane clearing before each reversal, and a navigable graph kept strongly connected at all times. An action-resolution algorithm grounded in graph orientation theory admits a proposal closing a direction only if the network stays strongly connected and otherwise relaxes or reverts it, keeping all junctions mutually reachable within the model, even during clearing. All road controllers share one transformer whose attention, Global Endpoint Relation-Aware Spatio-Temporal Self-Attention (GERASTSA), spans all road-time tokens, biased by the endpoint relations between roads. It is pretrained on action-conditioned traffic forecasting and fine-tuned with per-road proximal policy optimization under a mixed reward that also credits neighboring roads and the network. On a 6 x 6 grid with commuter rush hours, the learned policy makes about two thirds of roads one-way in the peak direction and cuts daily delay by 90% against the initial configuration held fixed and by 85% against a tuned two-way load balancer. Restricted to two-way roads at test time, it gains only about as much as this balancer, whereas its learned speed limits add delay. Pretraining roughly halves the updates needed to surpass the fixed configuration. Of the ablations, only removing the relational bias or the spatial embedding clearly matters, multiplying delay about fivefold.

papers.title: Uncovering Shortcut Amplification in Video RLVR through the Lens of Perceptual Uncertainty Collapse
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as an effective post-training paradigm for enhancing the video reasoning capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs). Despite its empirical effectiveness, we show that outcome-level optimization can introduce an undesirable shortcut amplification effect, whereby models increasingly favor text-prior answers even when they are not supported by the visual evidence. To characterize this behavior, we investigate the training dynamics of video RLVR through the lens of perceptual uncertainty, analyzing how predictive uncertainty evolves under video-conditioned and text-only contexts. Our analysis identifies a perceptual uncertainty collapse phenomenon, in which RL training continuously sharpens the model's answer distribution while the uncertainty reduction attributable to visual evidence progressively diminishes. A further gradient-direction analysis reveals that such confidence enhancement becomes increasingly less aligned with visually grounded uncertainty reduction and is instead dominated by text-prior compression. Motivated by these findings, we propose Bifocal Self-distillation Policy Optimization (BSPO), a self-distillation framework that regulates policy updates with two complementary distributional signals. Specifically, BSPO derives empirical reasoning principles from intra-group correct and incorrect rollouts to identify reasoning-sensitive tokens, and introduces shortcut-aware visual perturbation to penalize predictions that remain invariant when task-relevant visual evidence is weakened. By adaptively reweighting the original RL advantage, BSPO preserves the task-solving benefits of RLVR while promoting updates that are both reasoning-sensitive and visually grounded. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of BSPO in improving video reasoning performance and strengthening visual faithfulness.

papers.title: Latent Visual Contrastive Reasoning with Multi-Branch Exploration
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models have made substantial progress in visual question answering, but complex visual reasoning often requires locating and comparing multiple pieces of question-relevant visual evidence. Existing methods that move intermediate reasoning into the visual latent space usually follow a single linear reasoning trajectory, which can be limiting when multiple visual hypotheses or competing evidence regions are relevant. We propose Latent Visual Contrastive Reasoning, a branch-aware latent reasoning framework that generates multiple question-conditioned latent visual branches as soft hypotheses over image tokens. To train these branches, our method uses bounding-box evidence annotations to build target evidence representations and introduces a soft contrastive branch-evidence alignment objective. This objective encourages evidence-relevant branches to align with annotated visual regions while contrasting them against negative evidence. We instantiate our method on Qwen2.5-VL backbones and train it with standard supervised fine-tuning. Experiments on perception-intensive visual reasoning benchmarks show that the proposed method achieves overall improvements over the corresponding backbone and single-path latent reasoning baselines at both 3B and 7B scales.

papers.title: When Visual Evidence Is Insufficient: How Instructions, Post-Training, and Internal Activations Shape Refusal in Multimodal Language Models
papers.abstract_en: For reliable deployment, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) should recognize when an image provides insufficient evidence to answer a question and withhold unsupported answers. Yet refusal alone is not necessarily evidence of such recognition: models may refuse because of unrelated safety constraints or without identifying the missing evidence. We study how refusal on visually unanswerable questions is shaped by three sources of control: inference-time instructions, post-training, and internal activation interventions. Across three MLLMs on the MoHoBench benchmark, we systematically manipulate the meaning and placement of refusal instructions, compare supervised and preference-based post-training, and intervene on a refusal-related activation direction derived from naturally answered and refused examples. We find that refusal is highly sensitive to both the meaning and placement of instructions, with model-specific changes at the sample level that are obscured by aggregate refusal rates. Evidence-aware and general refusal instructions have stronger effects than an intentionally mismatched safety instruction. Post-training produces larger increases in refusal, but can also induce responses that combine refusal language with attempted answers. In contrast, activation intervention produces smaller yet transferable changes across prompt conditions, without evidence of indiscriminate refusal on tested visually answerable samples. These findings show that refusal is jointly shaped by external instructions, post-training, and internal representations, highlighting the need to disentangle evidence recognition from a model's learned propensity to refuse.

papers.title: HiLo-RD: Cross-Budget Self-Distillation for Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract_en: We propose HiLo-RD (High-to-Low Budget Representation Distillation) to improve masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) under a limited generation budget. Unlike autoregressive models, MDLMs choose both what to generate and where to commit it. This creates two coupled challenges: predicting useful content before reasoning is complete, and deciding when to fix answer tokens that shape later predictions. We identify budget-induced premature commitment: even when a correct solution fits, the model can fix answer fragments near the window boundary before resolving intermediate steps. These fragments become context for later predictions and redirect subsequent reasoning. Existing post-training methods do not directly transfer the stronger trajectories that the same model follows with a larger window. HiLo-RD addresses this gap by (1) pairing large-window teacher states with cropped small-window views and (2) matching their hidden representations at committed positions. This supervision guides both token prediction and commitment order without an external teacher. Across mathematics benchmarks, HiLo-RD improves low-budget accuracy and shortens responses; these gains extend to code generation without code-domain training. On GSM8K, accuracy rises by 9.4 percentage points as mean readable length falls by about 25%. Attention diagnostics and fixed-budget order interventions support the proposed mechanism. Together, these results show that large-window reasoning can improve small-window decoding.

papers.title: When All Rollouts Fail: Policy-Compatible Joint Decoding for Hard-Problem Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) derives its learning signal from binary rewards via on-policy exploration and becomes a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning of large language models. Yet it faces a learning cliff on problems beyond model's current ability: when every rollout fails, the samples reveal nothing about a correct solution, and group-relative estimators (e.g., GRPO, RLOO) collapse the update to zero advantage. Expert trajectories offer a remedy, but they are incompatible with the current policy and often lie in the student's low-probability regions, so the surviving updates demand large parameter shifts and decay into surface-level imitation rather than transferable reasoning. We argue that a useful learning signal on hard problems must be both verifiably correct and sufficiently compatible with the current policy. We propose Policy-Compatible Reinforcement Learning (PICO), which performs distribution-constrained joint decoding: expert data guides decoding at the token level while preserving the student's relative token probabilities, and a dynamic top-k mechanism confines the sampling distribution under a finite divergence budget, yielding trajectories that are verified and policy-compatible by construction. These trajectories are optimized jointly with on-policy rollouts under a mixed-behavior objective that mitigates their distribution mismatch via importance sampling. Experiments across reasoning diverse datasets and agentic benchmarks demonstrate that PICO consistently outperforms standard RLVR and prior off-policy baselines.

papers.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion language models offer a promising path to efficient agents through parallel token generation. However, efficient interaction requires adapting both where computation is spent and how much text is generated. We introduce a metacognitive controller that guides diffusion generation according to the needs of the current response and the agent's interaction with the environment. It learns when to finalize tokens and how far generation should extend, reducing overall computation within responses. Our controller, a lightweight plug-in for the diffusion backbone, is trained on agent trajectories to balance correctness and generation cost. This approach connects the agent's generation process to the interaction the agent serves. Experiments across five benchmarks demonstrate that our approach reduces inference FLOPs by 20.6% on average compared with the most efficient baseline, while maintaining competitive task accuracy. Ablation studies further validate the effectiveness of our approach.

papers.title: 3D-SceneQ: Empowering 3D LLM With Query-Guided Adaptive Pruning and Multi-Modal Feature Enhancement
papers.abstract_en: Current 3D scene understanding pipelines typically concatenate vast numbers of 3D object tokens with text tokens and feed the resulting sequence to a Large Language Model (LLM). However, existing 3D-LLMs for scene understanding encounter two major limitations: (i) excessive inclusion of task-irrelevant object data, introducing noise that reduces reasoning accuracy and increases hallucinations; and (ii) reliance solely on point cloud data, which inherently lacks the rich semantic information available in complementary 2D modalities, such as color, material properties, texture, and high-level contextual relationships. To address these challenges, we introduce 3D-SceneQ, a 3D LLM that unifies adaptive token pruning with multimodal semantic enrichment, markedly advancing scene understanding, reasoning, and grounding. Specifically, we propose a Query-Guided Adaptive Pruning (QGAP) module that adaptively selects task-relevant objects based on the intended meaning of user instructions, leveraging a learnable latent query to retain critical information while effectively suppressing irrelevant noise. In addition, we introduce a Multi-modal Object-level Feature Enhancement (MOFE) module, which integrates 2D feature embeddings from pre-trained models into 3D representation to enrich object-level semantic information. Evaluations show that 3D-SceneQ outperforms current state-of-the-art methods across multiple benchmarks (e.g., +5.7 CIDEr on Scan2Cap and +17.0 EM@1 on SQA3D), demonstrating its remarkable capabilities in various 3D language reasoning tasks.

papers.title: GUI-JEPA: Candidate-Conditioned JEPA Latents as a Fast Action Policy for Mobile GUI Agents
papers.abstract_en: Mobile GUI agents are typically fine-tuned 7B-scale vision-language models (VLMs) that generate each action as text. However, these VLMs decode every action token by token, and even agents that score candidate actions keep a large language model or VLM in the loop, making them slow and memory-hungry. To address these issues, we propose GUI-JEPA, to our knowledge the first decoder-free GUI agent policy built on a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA), which selects actions in the latent space of a JEPA encoder pretrained on unlabelled GUI screenshots. Its action- and region-conditioned latent predictor turns the screen latent into one latent per candidate action, letting lightweight heads score all candidates against the instruction in a single batched pass, without decoding a token. We further show that the scorer relies on this latent pathway and that the predictor is trained for the decision itself: a randomly initialised predictor does just as well as one pretrained on screen dynamics. On AndroidControl, GUI-JEPA is 2.8-4.0x faster on the same GPU than a Qwen2.5-VL-7B agent we fine-tune with the same inputs, while reaching 86-92% of its in-distribution accuracy with 6% of its parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/bcwang-sjtu/GUI-JEPA

papers.title: Learning Where to Trust: Reliability-Guided Expert Routing and Velocity Gating for 3D Deformable Registration
papers.abstract_en: Deformable image registration relies on accurate anatomical correspondences. However, explicitly coupling local matching reliability with spatial context selection and deformation update strength remains insufficiently explored in learning-based registration. This challenge is particularly pronounced in homogeneous, weakly textured, and severely deformed regions, where ambiguous matches may induce erroneous deformation updates. We propose ReliMorph, a reliability-routed symmetric framework for 3D deformable registration that couples correspondence assessment with spatial context selection and update strength.Local correlation distributions characterize correspondence ambiguity using shared anatomical features with modality-specific adaptation. These reliability cues guide spatial expert fusion and gate residual velocities during coarse-to-fine refinement. Updated inverse-inconsistency feedback guides routing and gating at finer pyramid levels. To our knowledge, ReliMorph is the first 3D deformable registration framework to jointly condition spatial expert routing and residual velocity gating on correspondence reliability. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ReliMorph consistently outperforms competing methods in anatomical overlap, highlighting its effectiveness across unimodal and multimodal registration tasks.

papers.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
papers.abstract_en: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. How these different kinds of knowledge are learned as pretraining progresses remains unclear. Recent point-in-time models trained on web snapshots from different years provide a way to probe how knowledge prevalence varies over time. Using these models, we propose a temporal variability score (TVS), defined as the coefficient of variation of an item's negative log-likelihood across models. A higher score suggests that the knowledge may be less consistently represented across years of web text. We evaluate six benchmarks covering diverse topics using six models from multiple open-source model families. We find that low- and high-TVS items are learned similarly early in training, but high-TVS items improve faster later on. At the end of the pretraining run, high-TVS items outperform low-TVS items in 34 of 36 model-benchmark settings, with an average advantage of 7.3 points of chance-normalized accuracy. This pattern is most robust on knowledge-intensive tasks, even when comparing items of similar difficulty. Our findings reveal differences in how knowledge is learned over the course of pretraining, with temporal variability providing a diagnostic of these learning dynamics beyond aggregate benchmark scores.

papers.title: RankFormer: Rethinking Time Series Transformers through Representation Capacity Analysis and Progressive Decoding
papers.abstract_en: Multivariate time series forecasting plays a critical role in Web and cyber-physical systems, where large-scale services and IoT infrastructures generate complex temporal data. Transformer-based models have achieved strong empirical performance in this domain, yet the principles governing the expressive capacity of their learned representations remain insufficiently understood. Moreover, many existing models rely on simplified decoding strategies, including channel-independent modeling and direct projection heads, which limit their ability to capture complex multivariate dynamics. To address these challenges, we propose RankFormer, a novel encoder-decoder architecture for multivariate time series forecasting. We establish a rank-based analysis framework to investigate how tokenization, embedding, and attention designs affect the representation capacity of time series Transformers. Our analysis reveals that patchification increases the potential representation capacity by aggregating multiple temporal observations into each token, while subsequent encoding operations determine how much of this capacity is realized. Guided by these insights, we develop a rank-enhancing encoder with Hourglass Attention to improve rank stability during information interaction. Furthermore, we introduce the Interactive Progressive Decoder (IPD), which improves future trajectory modeling through global-guided cross-channel interaction and progressive refinement. Extensive experiments on real-world long-term forecasting benchmarks demonstrate that RankFormer achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art methods. Code repository: https://github.com/TangPeiwang/Rankformer.

papers.title: SpecLST: Spectral-Enhanced Long-Short Term Spatio-Temporal Multimodal Modeling for Traffic Forecasting
papers.abstract_en: Modeling multi-scale dynamics in urban road networks is essential for intelligent transportation systems but is often hindered by the computational cost of long-range historical context and the challenge of fusing heterogeneous modalities. Existing spatio-temporal frameworks face a trade-off between sequence length and memory overhead, while frequently neglecting the transient effects of exogenous factors such as road incidents and weather. To address these limitations, we propose SpecLST, a frequency-enhanced long-short-term spatio-temporal multimodal framework. SpecLST leverages a fast Fourier transform-based frequency-domain representation module to efficiently encode multi-week historical dependencies, bypassing the memory bottlenecks of standard attention mechanisms over raw long sequences. Heterogeneous context is integrated through attention-based fusion, followed by a sparse Mixture-of-Experts backbone with graph augmentation for spatio-temporal representation learning. Additionally, a frequency-enhanced residual head isolates high-frequency transients, improving sensitivity to abrupt traffic anomalies. At the 60-minute horizon, SpecLST achieves mean relative error reductions of 14.10% in MAE, 10.35% in RMSE, and 15.78% in MAPE across eight neural forecasting baselines and four datasets, with the dataset- and metric-specific average reductions ranging from 5.63% to 22.21%.

papers.title: Clearing the FoG: Training KG Agents to Retrieve the Evidence Behind Their Answers
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) can answer many factual questions correctly, but a correct answer is not necessarily a supported one. For an LLM agent, a knowledge graph (KG) plays two roles: as a source of answers, it supplies facts that the model lacks; as a source of evidence, it supplies the supporting triples that make an answer traceable and auditable. However, existing KG agents treat the KG only as a source of answers: their training data carries answers but not evidence, and their training rewards check the answer but not the retrieved evidence, so agents often answer correctly without retrieving the supporting triples. We propose FoG, a framework that trains KG agents to retrieve the evidence behind their answers. FoG consists of evidence-grounded synthesis, a KG interaction agent, and an evidence-coverage process reward (ECPR): the synthesis recursively hides explicit entities behind verifiable sub-questions, so that every question carries its supporting triples by construction; the agent records the triples returned by the KG; and ECPR credits each supporting triple to the turn that first retrieves it. Experiments on three KGQA benchmarks demonstrate that FoG enables 3B--4B open-source agents to outperform substantially larger baselines in answer accuracy and evidence coverage, with zero-shot cross-KG transfer.

papers.title: Less is more: learning what to profile for GPU kernel optimization
papers.abstract_en: Large language models have recently shown strong potential for automatically optimizing GPU kernels, yet their effectiveness depends critically on the hardware information available to the kernel optimization model. Existing systems typically rely on predefined profiling strategies, leaving what to profile largely outside the optimization process. We show that effective profiling is not simply about collecting more information: increasing the number of profiling metrics does not monotonically improve kernel optimization, while the most useful profiling information varies across kernels. Our theoretical analysis further shows that, under such heterogeneous profiling utility, kernel-conditioned selection can outperform any single fixed profiling configuration. Motivated by this observation, we propose AutoProfiler, a feedback-driven framework for learning a deterministic profiling tree from optimization feedback. The tree is iteratively refined through REWRITE and SPLIT operations, with an LLM generating candidate modifications and empirical evaluation determining their acceptance. Once constructed, the tree quickly gathers the required profiling information for any kernel, allowing the LLM rewriter to be invoked only once. Experiments on KernelBench show that our approach improves kernel optimization over fixed profiling configurations under constrained profiling budgets. These results suggest that hardware profiling should evolve from static metric collection toward profiling reasoning, making profiling itself a new dimension for improving kernel optimization. The codes are available at https://github.com/Satissss/AutoProfiler.

papers.title: EvoRouter: Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Routing via Insight-Guided On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract_en: Serving web queries at scale with multi-agent systems requires jointly configuring large language models, collaboration modes, agent counts, interaction rounds, and skills. However, the resulting configuration space grows combinatorially, while sparse execution rewards provide limited fine-grained supervision for interdependent planning decisions. We propose EvoRouter, a self-evolving multi-agent routing framework driven by insight-guided on-policy distillation. A dedicated expert periodically synthesizes performance-cost feedback from configuration trajectories across tasks into reusable conditional routing insights about capability requirements, returns from resource scaling, and interactions among configuration choices. A privileged teacher combines these evolving insights with current execution feedback to provide dense token-level supervision for the router's own planning trajectories through on-policy distillation. Cost-aware reinforcement learning jointly optimizes task performance and computational cost. Together, these training signals internalize execution insights into the routing policy. The updated policy generates new trajectories that support subsequent insight extraction, forming an execution-driven self-improvement loop. We evaluate EvoRouter on 19 in-domain datasets spanning five domains and two out-of-domain benchmarks. EvoRouter achieves an average in-domain accuracy of 68.69%, outperforming the strongest routing baseline by 7.23 percentage points while reducing inference compute cost by 50.95%. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/CenYangtze/EvoRouter.

papers.title: SimPOTrans: Self-Adaptation for Offline-to-Simultaneous Speech Translation via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Simultaneous speech translation (SimulST) aims to translate ongoing speech with low latency while preserving translation quality. Recent studies have adopted large language models (LLMs) for SimulST and formulated it as a multi-turn dialogue task for efficient generation, achieving state-of-the-art performance. However, existing dialogue-style SimulST approaches typically rely on specialized training schemes to acquire simultaneous translation behavior, either using synthesized read/write trajectories, which may provide suboptimal training signals, or jointly optimizing translation quality and latency, whose competing objectives may cause optimization instability. In this paper, we introduce SimPOTrans, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework that enables offline speech translation models to self-adapt to dialogue-style SimulST. Through a simple two-stage RL post-training pipeline, SimPOTrans rewards an offline model for exhibiting translation behaviors beneficial to simultaneous scenarios when given partial speech inputs, thereby enabling offline-to-simultaneous self-adaptation without synthesized read/write trajectories or explicit latency optimization. At inference time, SimPOTrans requires no external decision policy and enables flexible quality--latency control by simply adjusting the chunk size of speech input. Experiments on the ACL 60/60 and MCIF benchmarks across three language directions (En$\rightarrow$De, En$\rightarrow$Zh, and En$\rightarrow$Ja) demonstrate that SimPOTrans outperforms several strong baselines, achieving a superior quality--latency trade-off.

papers.title: Bayes-Adaptive MDPs for Rollout Allocation to Enhance GRPO Training
papers.abstract_en: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has demonstrated strong performance in LLM post-training. However, it allocates a uniform rollout budget to every training question, ignoring variations in question difficulty. As a result, highly difficult questions may receive too few rollouts to generate informative positive reward signals, limiting their contribution to training, while moderately difficult questions often receive more rollouts than necessary. In this work, we formulate the problem of difficulty-aware rollout budget allocation to maximize training utility under the same total rollout budget as standard GRPO. We propose AdaRoll-GRPO, which reformulates rollout allocation as a sequential decision-making problem and leverages a Bayes-adaptive Markov decision process (MDP) to learn an adaptive allocation policy. The learned policy is computed offline and applied during GRPO training without introducing additional online optimization overhead. Extensive experiments on multiple reasoning datasets and LLM architectures demonstrate that AdaRoll-GRPO consistently improves GRPO training performance under a fixed rollout budget, highlighting the effectiveness of adaptive rollout allocation for GRPO in LLM post-training.

papers.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal perception forms the foundation of multimodal intelligence. In particular, spatial perception and multimodal long-context understanding are two pivotal tasks that underpin embodied AI and multimodal agents. However, synthesizing targeted, high-quality training data for these tasks remains difficult and costly. Our key insight is that these tasks share an underlying capability, which we call connecting evidence: identifying relevant visual facts, binding them to the correct entities, recovering their relations, and composing them into an answer. Crucially, targeted training data are far easier to synthesize for this capability than for these tasks themselves. To strengthen this capability, we propose EvidenceConnect, an easy-to-implement data synthesis framework that uses zoomed views of related regions within a single image to generate questions requiring comparison, aggregation, or chaining of visual evidence. To ensure quality, a reference answer is retained only when independent VLMs agree on it, and region-ablation tests discard questions whose answer survives the removal of selected regions. We then train base VLMs on the resulting data with RLVR, obtaining Zooming without Zooming v2 (ZwZ2). Although the synthesized data are not tailored to any downstream benchmark, ZwZ2 improves fine-grained and spatial perception, with further gains on embodied spatial reasoning, multimodal long-context understanding, multimodal agent tasks, and general visual reasoning. These results establish EvidenceConnect as an effective framework for supervising evidence connection and suggest that strengthening this shared capability leads to more generalizable multimodal perception.

papers.title: Learning from Points and Patches: A Pre-trained Hybrid Attention Transformer for Time Series Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Time-series data generated by Web services and connected systems support applications such as user activity analysis, service monitoring, and resource management. However, learning transferable representations from heterogeneous time series remains challenging due to diverse temporal patterns, variable sequence lengths, and limited high-quality annotations. Despite the success of pre-training in natural language processing and computer vision, effective time-series pre-training requires strategies tailored to temporal data. We propose TimeHAT (Hybrid Attention Transformer), a general-purpose pre-training framework for time-series analysis that addresses two complementary questions: what to learn and how to learn. For what to learn, we introduce a Unified Point-Patch Masking Strategy (UPPMS) that integrates point-level and patch-level supervision within a unified framework for contextual reconstruction and causal extrapolation, enabling the model to capture both fine-grained temporal variations and broader temporal patterns. For how to learn, we develop a Hybrid Attention Encoder (HAE) that combines prefix-constrained bidirectional attention in initial layers with directional hybrid attention in deeper layers, aiming to preserve effective contextual interactions while mitigating rank degeneration. We evaluate TimeHAT across real-world datasets and four downstream tasks: classification, long-term forecasting, imputation, and anomaly detection. Experiments cover fine-tuning, few-shot, and zero-shot transfer settings, demonstrating competitive performance across diverse time-series analysis tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/TangPeiwang/TimeHAT.

papers.title: ACSAN: All-Convolutional Self-Attention Network Integrating Convolutional Operations with Vision Transformer
papers.abstract_en: In the past few years, Vision Transformer (ViT) has achieved excellent performance in the field of computer vision. However, there still some problems remain. For instance, ViTs heavily rely on large-scale training data since they simply contain a large number of trainable parameters, which slows down their learning efficiency and limits their applicability in resource-constrained scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning model, namely All-Convolutional Self-Attention Network (ACSAN), which applies convolution operations to replace fully-connected matrices multiplications in the ViT framework. To implement ACSAN, we firstly design Dynamic Convolutional Self-Attention (DCSA) as the basic module, which employs multi-scale dilated convolutions to generate Query, Key, and Value. We defined spatial self-attention and channel self-attention to generate attention features respectively. The two attention features are finally merged as the output of the DCSA module. Based on DCSA, we then construct the basic ACSAN block. Comparing with ViT, we use DCSA to replace the regular self-attention operations, and use convolution layers to replace MLPs. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we train ACSAN on three widely-used image classification databases, i.e. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet-1k, from scratch. Experimental results show that ACSAN achieves excellent classification accuracy comparing with standard ViT with comparable or fewer parameters, as well as other state-of-the-art methods. Ablation studies verify that each component contributes positively to the final performance.

papers.title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Embedding-level scaling expands the capacity of language models through lookup-based memory rather than by increasing model depth, width, or dense computation. Extending this idea to vision-language models (VLMs) is challenging because visual features are continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent, unlike discrete text tokens that naturally support n-gram lookup. We introduce V-LUMEN, a visual lookup memory for VLMs. V-LUMEN discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys through spatial aggregation-based hashing, and modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals; all addressing is non-parametric, and the retrieved embeddings are fused into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks, V-LUMEN substantially improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data. At a matched parameter budget, moving part of a LoRA or MoE adapter's capacity into V-LUMEN preserves accuracy on two backbones, indicating that external visual memory is an independent capacity axis rather than a stronger adaptation method. Because lookup cost is constant in table size and incurred only once at prefill, this capacity grows in storage rather than in per-token compute. Code is available at https://github.com/miso-choi/V-Lumen.

papers.title: MemVLN: Streaming Episodic Memory for Vision-Language Navigation
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to follow language instructions through 3D environments. Maintaining persistent episodic memory remains a challenge for VLM-based streaming agents in long-horizon navigation. We present MEMVLN, a streaming episodic memory framework that maintains a bounded bank of compressed perceptual features annotated with timesteps and action-derived relative poses, and produces compact memory tokens via cross-attention. We pair the proposed memory with a frozen pretrained geometry encoder. To learn the memory module, we design a masking-based trajectory summarization task with multi-granularity sub-trajectory decomposition, encouraging route reconstruction exclusively from episodic memory. Under navigation training restricted to the official R2R/RxR trajectories, MEMVLN achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics on standard VLN-CE benchmarks. Long-horizon analyses further characterize when episodic memory is useful. For physical evaluation, we collect 30 instruction-conditioned episodes in one physical scene, use 24 as demonstrations for post-training, and hold out six for testing. On the held-out episodes, MEMVLN improves success over the VLM baseline from 17% to 40%, and post-training further raises it to 47%.

papers.title: SplatScout: Query-Driven Part-Level Referring Segmentation in Gaussian Scenes
papers.abstract_en: Existing referring segmentation methods on Gaussian scenes primarily target whole objects, relying on segmenter-generated candidates from which a vision-language model (VLM) selects. Such predetermined fixed candidates may omit fine-grained parts needed as targets or cues for identifying objects. We introduce SplatScout, a query-driven, closed-loop approach that places perception under VLM control. The model actively selects views, directs segmentation, and inspects rendered 3D results to refine its predictions. For part-level evaluation, we introduce PartRef-ScanNet++, comprising 261 manually verified queries across 12 ScanNet++ scenes with mesh-derived ground truth. On PartRef-ScanNet++, SplatScout achieves 0.538 mIoU, substantially outperforming existing methods. Ablations demonstrate the benefits of iterative refinement, while comparisons across VLM backbones highlight the importance of effective tool-feedback utilization. SplatScout also achieves higher scores on four existing referring benchmarks. Code and the PartRef-ScanNet++ benchmark are available at https://github.com/kaust-violab/SplatScout.

papers.title: Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning for Dyadic Relationship Recognition
papers.abstract_en: Dyadic relationship recognition aims to identify the latent social relationship between two individuals from their multimodal interactions. Existing methods typically project heterogeneous cues into a shared representation and optimise a flat classification objective, overlooking that relationships may rely on different interaction patterns. For instance, distant relationships can often be inferred from direct behavioural correspondence, whereas close relationships are better reflected by coordinated affective, behavioural, and multimodal responses. To address this limitation, we propose HiRe-DRR, a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning framework that organises relationship evidence from three complementary perspectives: feature level, interaction type, and relationship hierarchy. HiRe-DRR decomposes facial, bodily, acoustic, and textual cues into low- and high-level representations and constructs homogeneous and heterogeneous cross-participant interactions. We further introduce the Mixture-of-Interaction Transformer (MoI-Former), which treats diverse interactions as specialised experts and employs relation-aware sparse routing to identify relationship-relevant evidence while preserving contextual interaction information. The proposed Hierarchical Conditional Loss (HC-Loss) exploits the hierarchical nature of social relationships through coarse-to-fine supervision, enabling structured relationship reasoning. Extensive experiments on three dyadic relationship benchmarks demonstrate that HiRe-DRR outperforms recent representative image-, video-, and multimodal methods. Our routing analysis further reveals that distant relationships tend to rely on low-level homogeneous interactions, whereas closer relationships focus on high-level heterogeneous interactions. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tw-repository/HiRe-DRR.

papers.title: LEAP: a Latent Embedding Anomaly Patch-Transformer for time-series anomaly detection
papers.abstract_en: Time-series anomaly detection is dominated by reconstruction-based neural detectors, whose objective is structurally flawed. Since the target is also the input, an expressive model can learn to reconstruct anomalies too, leaving uninformative residuals. Recent large-scale benchmarks show that, on curated data, elaborate deep detectors rarely beat simple statistical baselines, while current leaders rely on representation learning. We propose LEAP (Latent Embedding Anomaly Patch-Transformer), which combines masked prediction with latent representation-based anomaly evidence, without relying on reconstruction or attention-based scoring. The model removes patches from a window and predicts them from the remaining temporal and cross-channel context, so prediction errors measure how well learned dynamics explain hidden segments. Deterministic complementary group masking ensures every time step is scored while hidden, with identical visible fractions during training and inference. LEAP adds three label-free evidence sources: latent-embedding novelty calibrated by local density, local temporal contrast, and per-channel novelty pooled over channels selected by six label-free criteria. Under the TSB-AD protocol, the full model achieves a VUS-PR of $0.5179 \pm 0.0022$ on $180$ held-out multivariate series. On TSB-AD-U, a univariate variant combining multi-scale masked-prediction scoring with latent novelty, without contrast or channel-pool novelty, achieves $0.6194 \pm 0.0016$ on $350$ held-out series. Both results average three random seeds. A five-stage ablation on TSB-AD-M, supported by paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, shows statistically significant gains from each successive component.

papers.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
papers.abstract_en: We introduce Heads of Security (HoS), a prompt injection defense that enforces instruction-data separation via a small set of learned per-head attention gates. HoS learns how each head should redistribute attention between trusted and untrusted tokens, enabling models to reason over untrusted content without following injected instructions. We evaluate HoS on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B. We compare it against SecAlign++, a state-of-the-art finetuning-based defense, and ASIDE, a defense that, like ours, builds instruction-data separation into the model architecture. We show that HoS offers greater robustness to adaptive attacks, better performance on standard utility benchmarks, and matches top performance on standard agentic prompt injection benchmarks. More specifically, the black-box RL-Hammer attack reaches 97% ASR against GPT-OSS-20B and 85% against SecAlign, but only 10% against HoS. Claudini, a state-of-the-art white-box attack, strengthened against HoS through autoresearch, requires 3 times more FLOPs to reach the same ASR on HoS as it does on GPT-OSS-20B or SecAlign. HoS preserves base-model utility across standard multiple-choice benchmarks and prompting setups, whereas SecAlign and ASIDE degrade in few-shot settings. On agentic benchmarks with static attacks, HoS and SecAlign perform similarly and substantially improve the security-utility trade-off over the base model. ASIDE struggles with tool use, achieving only 10% utility. These results show that prompt injection robustness can be achieved and improved through targeted attention interventions.

papers.title: Which Hand Was Late? Diagnosis for Robot Failure Recovery in Bimanual Tool Use
papers.abstract_en: Failure diagnosers for robot manipulation are increasingly vision--language models (VLMs), trained and evaluated on single-arm failures produced by perturbing a successful demonstration. Bimanual tool use adds failures of other kinds: a tool that slips out of its socket while still held, two correct gestures made at different times, and attempts that fail for two reasons at once. On a simulated bimanual tool-use task whose failure causes are read from the recorded trace, we measure what each sensing channel lets a diagnoser tell. The tool's slip is read on the tool hand; which hand was late is read on both arms, while a sensor on one hand reads its own hand's delay and at most part of the other's; and whether a late attempt was also pushed too weakly is not identifiable from passive sensing when the tool hand is late. Within two attempts, a repair policy that escalates when the cause is not identifiable repairs as many failures as one told the true cause. A VLM's internal state carries the late hand almost perfectly, along a direction no closer to the one its answer reads than a random one; whether the answer reports it depends on the wording of the question.
